chapter: On the road with Spivak and Sauter-Finegan
title: Stop playing that Chinese music, and playing to the style
summary: A joke about bebop in Spivak's band leads to his view that a player should fit the style of the band.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Isn’t that what Cab told Dizzy?

Yeah, yeah. I mean I do have opinions about that. I think if you’re playing in a Dixieland band you don’t play bebop. Some people feel they play the way they play no matter what they’re playing. I think you have to try to kind of style — maybe you’re prostituting yourself, I don’t think so. I think you have to kind of play the style of the music you’re playing in. You can’t get — but I kind of learned that as I got older. I think I can play in a Dixieland band and I think I can play creative in a simpler harmonic way and still be creative and be happy with myself. Naturally I’d rather play with music that’s a little more modern harmonically etc.
